blurb.en: A major El Niño; unusually wet short rains in much of Kenya.
The strongest El Niño on record with a strongly positive Indian Ocean Dipole — extreme short rains and widespread flooding that Kenyans still reference.
Failed short rains under borderline-weak La Niña conditions with a cool western Indian Ocean; severe pasture loss in the arid north.
Back-to-back failed seasons under La Niña — one of the region's worst droughts, with famine declared in parts of the Horn.
Failed short rains under a weak La Niña with a cool western Indian Ocean, followed by poor long rains — a national drought emergency was declared.

An exceptionally positive Indian Ocean Dipole — without a strong El Niño — brought extreme short rains, floods and, in their wake, the desert-locust upsurge. The clearest case that the IOD, not ENSO alone, carries Kenya's short rains.
Three consecutive La Niña years — five failed rainy seasons in a row. Pasture and harvests collapsed across the arid and semi-arid counties in Kenya's longest drought in decades.
El Niño with a positive IOD ended the long drought: heavy short rains (with serious flooding in November 2023) and a broad harvest recovery into 2024.
